disclosure: REAL transient (di/dt) IR-drop: OpenROAD PSM `analyze_power_grid -transient` performs the static DC operating point + a backward-Euler RC time-stepping solve under a vectorless per-clock triangular current model (quasi-static when no on-die capacitance is supplied). This is the BASE transient tier — the per-instance VECTORED DVD with a SAIF/VCD activity trace + package/board L·di/dt (RedHawk-SC / Voltus vectored) is the accuracy refinement tracked separately. The number is a genuine dynamic droop, not a static echo (a quasi-static solve yields ~2x the static drop).
static_from_transient_mv_null_because: NOT RECOVERABLE — and deliberately not restated. This field was published as 0.0002 by an emitter that forwarded the PSM transient report's static IR drop in VOLTS into a millivolt field (producer defect, fixed separately in dynamic_ir_vectored_emit.emit()). The obvious repair — multiply by 1000 and publish 0.2 mV — is WRONG, and was reverted after being caught: build_result applies round(x, 4) to this value, which at VOLT scale truncated it to ONE significant figure BEFORE it was ever stored. The digits are gone; scaling a destroyed value cannot restore them. This file's own surviving fields bound the truth: max_dynamic_drop_mv 0.485 (printed 4.85e-04 V, so the true value lies in [4.845e-4, 4.855e-4) V) and dynamic_static_ratio 2.00 (so the true ratio lies in [1.995, 2.005)) give static = dynamic/ratio in [0.24165, 0.24336] mV. The tool therefore printed 2.42e-04 or 2.43e-04 V. It cannot have printed 2.00e-04 V: that would have made the ratio line read 2.43, not 2.00. So 0.2 mV would be roughly 17% low. That derivation is an INTERVAL computed from this file, not a measurement, so no value is written into the field. The source PSM transient log is not in this deliverable, and this cell's campaign directory /home/reyerchu/campaign_v1565/spm/converge_1.5.65_sky130A (named as `project` by its own reports/orchestrator/phase2_one_shot.json) no longer exists, so the printed line cannot be retrieved. null with a reason, not a guess.
